response: Yes, older patients who refuse to participate in a self-management intervention in the Netherlands tend to differ from those who agree to participate. Research has shown that non-participants are often older, have more chronic conditions, experience more cognitive decline, and have lower levels of education and health literacy compared to participants. Additionally, non-participants may have more social isolation, poorer health status, and less confidence in managing their health. These differences can affect the generalizability of study results and highlight the need for tailored approaches to engage harder-to-reach older populations in self-management interventions.
